title: PARPi-GaMD — dual-system GaMD analysis of PARP1 inhibitor allosteric encoding: code, data and figures
description:
Replication package for a dual-system Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) study of PARP1 inhibitors. System S1 (catalytic domain only) quantifies the HD–ART sampled-range span; system S2 (near-full-length PARP1–DNA) quantifies protein–DNA and HD–ART collective variables, spanning ten inhibitors and a ligand-free control, extended by three audited protonation-state re-simulations (13 S1 and 13 S2 systems).

The analysis is framed as a six-diagnostic robustness audit of descriptor–phenotype rank associations: chemical-state assignment (with PROPKA-supported pKa audits), estimator dependence (cumulant / window-median / quantile / bootstrap estimators), sampling-window diagnostics with a calibrated noise floor, a planted-association positive-control benchmark, cross-docking RMSD validation against co-crystal structures, and exact-permutation small-panel association tests. The headline result is negative and is reported as such: with the chemically corrected five-inhibitor panel, no robust rank association between GaMD-derived descriptors and published trapping potency is established (rho = -0.205, exact p = 0.767; all panel variants and estimator conventions are covered in Tables S2, S4, S5, S13 and S14 of the companion manuscript).

The package contains the full analysis and figure code chains, the archived data layer (per-frame boost-energy series, reweighting weights, PMF curves, curated panel tables), the 27 manuscript figures (PDF + PNG), a per-artifact manifest mapping every manuscript number to its generating script, and the GaMD deployment record (builders, environment specifications, per-system deployment scripts).

Limitations of the study itself: the rank-association analyses operate on a five-inhibitor panel (exact permutation, n = 5), and the production simulations are 2-ns-window limited by design; the audit quantifies, rather than removes, that limitation. Raw production trajectories (~1 TB) are not distributed; the release contains the derived data layer and the tooling that regenerates every manuscript value.
